text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London pushed higher in light volume as commission houses bought the May contract, now spot position after the recent March expiry. A total 423 lots of white sugar, equivalent to 21,150 tonnes, was delivered against the March contract, with E.D.F.& Man buying everything from commission houses Prudential Bache and Refco. The ports specified were Rostock, Eemshaven and Immingham. May ended $3.10 higher at $304.60 per tonne, while August gained $2.90 to close at $304.60 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed higher across the board with front month March adding 14 points to close at 10.78 cents/lb, while May closed 13 points higher at 10.74 cents/lb. The outer months gained 9 points. The rise was ascribed to options-linked buying, but a round of speculative liquidation knocked the market off its highs ahead of the close. Raw sugar prices are again near the 11 cents/lb barrier and it will be interesting to see whether that can be breached. However, fundamentals remain bearish and only a few days ago the International Sugar Organization said that raw sugar prices could fall to 10 cents/lb.

CUBA - According to official sources Cuba's 1996/97 sugar harvest has suffered delays because of the late arrival of essential spare parts and imports like fertilizers, herbicides and pesticides as a result of the Helms-Burton legislation, which seeks to curb foreign investment in Cuba. While original hopes were for a crop of 5.2 to 5.3 million tonnes, after 4.5 million tonnes the previous year, official sources now expect only a 'modest' rise. Industry sources said on February 14 that Cuba has produced its first 1 million tonnes of sugar in the current 1996/97 harvest. Last year total production at the end of February was 1.753 million tonnes, raw value.

AUSTRALIA - Australia exported 269,727 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in December 1996, nearly 40 per cent less than was exported the same month the previous year. That brought total exports since the beginning of 1996/97 (June/December) up to 3.374 million tonnes, 2.2 per cent less than was exported the same period in 1995.

Raw sugar exports in June/December 1996 reached 2.238 million tonnes, down from 3.303 million tonnes the same period in 1995, while white sugar exports reached 125,007 tonnes, down from 135,594 tonnes shipped in June/December 1995.

Main countries of destination for Australian raw sugar in June/December 1996 were Canada (615,545 vs 462,227 tonnes), China (270,300 vs 317,614 tonnes), Japan (461,524 vs 614,315 tonnes), South Korea (562,669 vs 586,869 tonnes) and Malaysia (458,958 vs 539,713 tonnes). The main markets for Australian white sugar in June/December 1996 were Indonesia (20,704 vs 19,461 tonnes) and New Zealand (33,235 vs zero tonnes).

The Indian government has authorized the export of 250,000 tonnes of sugar in 1996/97 (October/September) the Commerce Ministry said. This includes 20,000 tonnes of sugar for export by the Indian Sugar and General Industry Export- Import Corporation (ISGIEC) to the European Union and the United States under existing preferential arrangements. This is the first export authorization since the government ended ISGIEC's monopoly over sugar exports in January.
